title: How I’m using Generative AI to create visual assets for a Japanese learning game with thousands of words
author: Thank_Japan
selftext:
Hi everyone! I wanted to share my workflow for my project **"Thank Japan"**, a web-based game for learning Japanese.

**The Challenge:**

The game covers the entire JLPT range (N5 to N1), which means I need thousands of unique visual aids to help learners associate kanji/vocabulary with real-life contexts. Hiring an artist for this volume was budget-prohibitive.

**The AI Workflow:**

I’m using generative AI to solve this. My workflow involves:

**Style Consistency:** I’ve developed specific prompting templates to maintain two distinct styles: "Anime-style" for daily actions/emotions, and "Photorealistic" for professional or cultural topics.

**Contextual Accuracy:** For Japanese culture-specific words (like "Matsutake" or "Koinobori"), I often have to iterate on prompts to ensure the AI understands the traditional Japanese aesthetic correctly.

**Integration:** These assets are served through a Django backend, paired with interactive quizzes.

**The Result:**

Using AI has allowed me to scale the content significantly faster than traditional methods. I can now provide a visual context for words that are usually just text in textbooks.

I’d love to hear from other devs: How do you handle style consistency when generating thousands of assets? Or if you have any feedback on the UI/UX for an educational game, I’m all ears!

Check it out: [https://www.thankjapan.com/](https://www.google.com/url?sa=E&q=https%3A%2F%2Fthankjapan.com%2F)

comments.author: Thank_Japan
comments.body:
Update: I fixed the flashbang! 🌑

You were right the culprit was the base template's CSS, which had a light grey background (#f3f4f6). It was flashing for a split second before the dark game theme loaded. I've now set the background to dark (#111) at the root HTML level, so transitions are perfectly smooth now!

I also simplified the main button to 'Play Japanese Quiz 🎮' to make it more intuitive. Thanks again for the sharp feedback, it really helped improve the UX!
[🔗ThankJapan.com](https://www.thankjapan.com/)
